service.title: Write Rate
service.tip: Cluster-wide writes per second across measure + stream + trace data models.

service.title: Query Rate
service.tip: Cluster-wide gRPC query calls per second seen at the liaison front door.

service.title: Error Rate
service.tip: Cluster-wide errors per minute (gRPC + registry + stream-msg + publish + sync-loop). Absent renders as 0 on a healthy cluster.

service.title: CPU Cores

service.title: Memory Used
service.tip: Total memory used across the cluster.

service.title: Disk Used
service.tip: Total on-disk bytes used across the cluster's data paths.

service.title: Cluster Throughput
service.tip: Write vs query rate over time.

service.title: Containers by Role
service.tip: Live container count per role (data / liaison), derived from the system uptime gauge. The lifecycle sidecar runs no system collector, so it never appears here.

instance.title: Time Since Last Sync
instance.tip: How long ago the last migration cycle started, e.g. "5m 20s ago". Appears once the first migration cycle has run.

instance.title: Last Sync
instance.tip: Whether the last migration cycle succeeded or failed.

instance.title: Migration Cycles
instance.tip: Cumulative tier-migration cycles run by the lifecycle sidecar.

instance.title: CPU Usage
instance.tip: Process CPU consumption in cores.

instance.title: GC Pause (avg)

instance.title: Uptime
instance.tip: Days since the node started. Absent on the lifecycle sidecar (no system collector).

instance.title: Disk Usage
instance.tip: Used / total across the node's data paths.

instance.title: Disk Used / Total
instance.tip: Used per data path, against total filesystem capacity. Paths sharing one filesystem report identical figures.

instance.title: Network I/O
instance.tip: Per-interface receive / send throughput.

instance.title: Query Rate by Service
instance.tip: gRPC query calls/s split by BanyanDB data-model service (measure / stream / trace / property).

instance.title: gRPC Errors / min
instance.tip: Sum of total + registry + stream-msg gRPC errors. Lazily registered — absent renders as 0 on a healthy liaison.

instance.title: Registry Ops / s
instance.tip: Schema-registry operations/s seen at the liaison front door.

instance.title: Write Rate
instance.tip: Writes/s seen at the liaison front door across the three data models.

instance.title: Publish Throughput
instance.tip: Tier-2 publish pipeline (liaison → data), broken out by operation.

instance.title: Publish p99 Latency
instance.tip: p99 send latency of the tier-2 publish pipeline, per operation.

instance.title: Part-sync Bytes
instance.tip: Bytes/s streamed to data nodes on the part-sync (file-sync) path. The queue_pub sent-bytes counter only ticks on chunked file-sync — regular write/query publishes are not counted here.

instance.title: Write Queue Pending
instance.tip: Liaison write-buffer depth: records buffered at the front door before publish.

instance.title: Publish Batch Throughput
instance.tip: Batches published/s by operation. Hidden until the cluster emits batch metrics.

instance.title: Stored Data Elements
instance.tip: Total file elements stored across measure + stream + trace.

instance.title: Write Queue (wqueue)
instance.tip: Data-node write queue: pending records, on-disk file parts, in-memory parts.

instance.title: Merge File Latency
instance.tip: Average on-disk file-merge latency per merge loop.

instance.title: Merge Parts / Loop
instance.tip: Average parts merged per on-disk merge loop.

instance.title: Inverted Index Rate
instance.tip: Series-index updates and term searches per second (measure + stream storage + stream tst).

instance.title: Index Documents

instance.title: Subscribe Throughput
instance.tip: Subscribe-side queue throughput by operation (query / file-sync / batch-write / control).

instance.title: Retention Disk Usage

instance.title: Subscribe Message Throughput
instance.tip: Per-record processing rate the subscriber unpacks from batches.

widgets.title: Trace Outcomes
widgets.tip: Retained + dropped account for the evaluated traces. Immature traces were never eligible — their fragments are still inside the maturity boundary, so they are not a sampling failure.

widgets.title: Active Samplers
widgets.tip: Sampler plugins registered per storage group. A group absent from this list has no pipeline — its traces are never evaluated, so nothing is dropped for it.

widgets.title: Drop Ratio by Group
widgets.tip: Committed drop ratio per storage group, per step — dropped over evaluated traces after BanyanDB's safety guards. Deliberately per group rather than one cluster headline: a cluster-wide card would be an unweighted mean of the per-step ratios, so a quiet minute would count as much as a busy one. A group below the others is usually explained by the safety events further down rather than by its rules.

widgets.title: Plugin Load Failures
widgets.tip: Plugin load failures per minute, by group, failing plugin and reason. Reconciliation fails open, so any value here means the chain is running WITHOUT a plugin the config asked for — sampling is not doing what it says. The plugin name and reason are only shown here.

widgets.title: Decide Rate by Result
widgets.tip: Decide() calls per second, per plugin and result. Alert on any panic, length_mismatch or late — they mean broken plugin behaviour or a call that outlived the merge timeout. decide_error may be transient.

widgets.title: Decide Latency
widgets.tip: Successful Decide() wall time per plugin — p99 takes the worst group, mean averages them. Derive a per-plugin SLO from a healthy baseline; an intentionally expensive plugin is not a fault.

widgets.title: Plugin Time per Trace
widgets.tip: Whole-chain plugin wall time per evaluated trace, per group — the sampling overhead paid on merge, over time. The upstream Grafana board splits this per plugin with PromQL's `group_left`; MAL has no equivalent, so the metric is the chain total and the per-plugin split lives in Decide Latency. Keep it comfortably below the data node's --trace-pipeline-decide-timeout (default 5s).

widgets.title: Chain Batches
widgets.tip: Chain batches per second by result. circuit_open means sampling is currently BYPASSED for that group; timeout is chain-level because the host can abandon the chain before a link returns. The traces each batch carried is the Batch Size p99 panel.

widgets.title: Batch Size p99
widgets.tip: p99 traces presented to the plugin chain per successful batch, per group. Read with Chain Batches: rate tells you how often the chain runs, this tells you how much it sees each time.

widgets.title: Sampler Rows
widgets.tip: Span / segment rows carried by evaluated traces, against the rows the samplers proposed dropping, broken out by the rule responsible. Same unit, so the two are directly comparable; the resulting share is the Dropped Row Ratio panel.

widgets.title: Sampler Decisions by Rule
widgets.tip: What the first-party samplers PROPOSED, attributed to the first matching rule — not what storage committed. A trace can be evaluated over several merge or finalization rounds, and the guards can retain a trace the plugin voted to drop, so read drop verdicts against Trace Outcomes.

widgets.title: Dropped Row Ratio
widgets.tip: Share of rows the samplers proposed dropping, per group. Proposed, not committed — the safety guards can retain a trace a plugin voted to drop. Treat it as incomplete whenever Row Count Unavailable is non-zero, since those traces are missing from the denominator.

widgets.title: Row Count Unavailable
widgets.tip: Trace evaluations whose metadata-only projection exposed no row count, per group. These traces are omitted from the row totals, so any non-zero value here means the Dropped Row Ratio is computed over an incomplete denominator.

widgets.title: Guard & Index Work
widgets.tip: Bloom-filter probes are the fragment guard checking for trace fragments outside the parts being merged; pruned entries are the secondary-index work a confirmed drop causes.

widgets.title: Safety Events
widgets.tip: Every series here RETAINS data a sampler proposed dropping. A drop ratio under target is explained here before it is explained by plugin logic.

widgets.title: Chain Errors by Reason
widgets.tip: Chain-level errors that forced fail-open retention of the whole batch.

widgets.title: Link Bypasses
widgets.tip: Individual links bypassed after decide_error, length_mismatch or panic. A chain batch can report success while one link was bypassed and its input retained — which is why this is separate from chain errors.

widgets.title: Registrations & Updates
widgets.tip: Pipeline registration, update and removal rate. A rejected result means OAP pushed a pipeline config the data node would not accept.

widgets.title: Drop-set Cap Impact
widgets.tip: The per-merge dropped-trace-ID set is memory-bounded. When it hits the ceiling the merge retains the rest — this is what makes a drop ratio plateau under load rather than tracking the rules.

widgets.title: Drop-set Size p99
widgets.tip: p99 dropped trace IDs held per merge lane. Read it against the Drop-set Budget panel: when the set outgrows the budget the merge stops accepting drops and retains the rest, which is what shows up as Drop-set Cap Impact.

widgets.title: Drop-set Budget
widgets.tip: Resolved per-merge memory budget for confirmed dropped trace IDs, per group — the ceiling the drop-set size runs into. Resolved per group, so groups can carry different budgets; a group with a smaller one reaches its ceiling first. Flat unless the data node is retuned.

widgets.title: Finalization Rounds
widgets.tip: Highest finalization round count observed across each group's cooled shards. Whether a shard has run out of rounds is the Finalization Terminal panel.

widgets.title: Finalization Terminal
widgets.tip: 1 when any cooled shard in the group is terminal and cannot run another finalization round — no more tail sampling will happen for that data, so whatever is stored is final. 0 otherwise. Charted over time so the transition is visible.

widgets.title: Plugin Telemetry Host Safety
widgets.tip: The host caps what a plugin may publish (100 label-value series per instrument) and rate-limits its logs. Non-zero means a plugin's OWN telemetry is truncated — the sampler decision metrics above are then incomplete, though sampling itself is unaffected.
